response.rationale: R8 is directly supported by two imaging spans confirming a porencephalic cyst and porencephalic area, which is the most specific and definitive diagnosis. R4 provides the inciting event (intracranial hemorrhage) but lacks direct confirmation of the resulting malformation. Other candidates are either non-specific signs (R2, R7) or have weak/contradicted evidence (R3, R6).

rejected.why: Microcephaly is a clinical sign, not a specific diagnosis; it is a consequence of the underlying brain malformation.
Micropolygyria is an associated cortical abnormality, not the primary diagnosis; it is part of the porencephalic syndrome.
CMV serology shows IgG positive/IgM negative, which is not diagnostic of active congenital infection; no other CMV-specific evidence is present.
Genetic disorder is contradicted by normal gene sequencing and metabolic screening; no supporting genetic evidence.
